title: France records 2,025 excess deaths at peak of heatwave as Europe braces for more extreme weather
facts: France recorded 2,025 excess deaths between June 22 and June 28 during a summer heatwave.
Mortality in France increased by nearly 30% during the final week of June compared to the prior week.
Stéphanie Rist serves as the French health minister.
Temperatures in Paris approached 41 degrees Celsius on June 24, 2026.
Mortality rose by 62% in the Paris region during the final week of June.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported that 72 people died from drowning since June 18.
Belgium recorded 1,222 excess deaths during the June heatwave.
Nearly half of the heatwave fatalities in Belgium occurred among individuals aged 85 and older.
Extreme heat caused approximately 480 excess deaths in the Netherlands.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu reported that nearly 7,000 fires broke out since the start of summer.
Approximately 8,700 hectares burned across France by early July.
A wildfire in Sainte-Marie-la-Mer and Canet-en-Roussillon prompted the evacuation of nearly 3,000 people.
The Portuguese government declared a national state of alert lasting until midnight on Tuesday.
Météo-France issued red alerts for forest fires in southern France.
The Copernicus climate service reported Europe is warming twice as fast as the global average.
